acceptance: Reproduce: from a linked worktree, a file-tool edit with a relative path changes the primary clone (record the mechanism: harness cwd vs worktree).

Make the failure mode fail closed before the write where the repository controls it (for example worktree-scoped tooling, a pre-tool check, or a member-create step that pins absolute paths), or document why the repo cannot control it and what the narrowest enforceable check is.
Detect writes to the primary within one agent step (not only at pr-preflight), with a test.
Guidance in docs/agent and the batch member brief template states absolute paths as a hard rule.
context:
Recurring incident across this session; backup of one stray diff at ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/primary-stray-backup/detector-member-stray.patch. Guardrail: never revert or clean the primary automatically; other sessions' edits must not be lost. Verification rubric: reproduce first; fix; regression test; comment-policy and ruff; PR merged with green CI and passing oracle review.

2026-11-11 evidence from a retrospective over 25 sessions (2026-10-18 to 2026-11-11): about 15 stray primary-clone edits or resets in one release session, 6 incidents that blocked every worker's preflight in another, and at least 5 more by delegated workers after #3888. The mechanism in every case: harness read, edit and grep tools resolve relative paths against the session directory (the primary clone) even after `cd` in bash, so `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in the shell reports the worktree while the edit lands in the primary clone. A read-side variant also occurs: relative reads return the primary clone's files, which lagged origin/develop by 30 to 195 commits in late October. A one-sentence AGENTS.md pointer was considered and does not fit the 17,300-byte instruction budget (21 bytes free); docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md already carries the worker rule and incidents continued, so a mechanical guard is the fix to pursue here.

Revalidated 2026-11-11 (origin/develop c7b75c80bc): still required; no mechanical guard has landed since. State today: PR #3888 (686b830432) report-only snapshot check (scripts/check_primary_clone_clean.sh, run from make pr-preflight; documented as a warning, not a failing gate, in docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md); PR #3957 (f8efe096c2) refuses primary-clone edits in a batch member's scope and member tracker writes before landing. PR #4054 is merged (f6f231c740, 2026-11-08) and is the privacy fix that the detector member produced, not a guard. Acceptance 4 is half done: docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md:44 ("Give workers absolute worktree paths") states the rule, but .claude/skills/todo/references/batch.md has no absolute-path rule for the member brief template. Acceptance 1-3 (reproduction, fail-closed or documented limit, detection within one agent step with a test) are untouched.

Recurrence 2026-11-11: a delegated subagent given an explicit worktree path (BenchBox.wt-fix-primitives-query-counts) made its first edits in the primary clone because the edit and write tools resolved relative paths against the session's working directory. It moved the edits into the worktree as a patch and restored the primary clone, which was confirmed clean. Related friction seen in the same run: `make agent-write-preflight` refuses a worktree created by the parent session ('owned by live session'), so each delegated worker needed `BENCHBOX_WORKTREE_TAKEOVER=1`, and the parent had to take the worktree back the same way to commit a review fix.

Owner decision 2026-11-12 (choice dialog): build a tool hook that refuses file-tool writes inside the primary clone, plus a failing check in agent-write-preflight as the backstop. If a harness cannot run such a hook, build the backstop and record the gap. Work started 2026-11-12 by the coordinating session; held so no other session claims it.

2026-11-12: PR #4143 open (head 8e691c38ad, branch fix/primary-clone-write-guard, worktree /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.wt-fix-primary-clone-write-guard): scripts/primary_clone_write_guard.py wired as a pre-tool hook for Claude Code, omp, Codex and Gemini CLI from tracked config; make agent-write-preflight fails when the primary's tracked files changed after the session snapshot. Not yet proven in a live harness session; a live test in a scratch clone and an independent review are running before arming. Left out: the batch member brief template lives in the skill catalog (joeharris76/skill-sync-skills skills/todo/references/batch.md), not in BenchBox.

2026-11-12: PR #4143 merged to develop as 4d0777d907 (verified an ancestor of origin/develop). Acceptance 1: mechanism reproduced in a scratch repository (file tools resolve relative paths against the session directory). Acceptance 2: scripts/primary_clone_write_guard.py refuses a file-tool write whose real target is inside the primary clone while a linked worktree exists; wired as a pre-tool hook for omp, Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI. Proven live in omp on the final design (relative write and relative edit blocked; absolute worktree edit, local:// and xd:// writes allowed; override honoured; applies inside subagents). Claude Code, Codex and Gemini are wired but unproven: they could not be run (expired login, usage limit, unsupported tier); Gemini also needs the workspace trusted; an open upstream issue reports Codex not enforcing a deny for apply_patch. Shell writes are not inspected. Acceptance 3: make agent-write-preflight fails when the primary's tracked files changed after the session's snapshot (per session; commit hooks only report), with tests. Acceptance 4: docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md and batch-feature-delivery.md state the rule; the member brief template lives in the skill catalog and is tracked as batch-member-brief-absolute-path-rule-in-catalog-20261112. The hook files are pinned by the instruction audit. The guard takes effect in a session only once the primary clone it starts in contains this commit.
description: The report-only guard from agent-relative-path-primary-clone-writes (PR #3888) did not stop recurrence. In three batches on 2026-11-07..09, delegated workers wrote to /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox through relative file-tool paths: the Spark-family leader (spark.py and its test, reverted with git apply -R), the plan-privacy detector member (anonymization.py and a test, restored by the controller from a backup), and a near miss in the publication batch (rejected). The edits were found only because batch tooling refused a dirty primary; each needed manual cleanup and owner authorization.
